decisions.reason: 和武憲皇后 is the posthumous name Hé-Wǔ-Xiàn (Hewuxian); Wuhe reverses 和 and 武. The proposed Empress Hewuxian matches the Chinese order and leaves the rest unchanged.
The literal’s Empress Wuhe likewise reverses 和武憲; Empress Hewuxian restores the correct posthumous-name reading without other changes.
謚曰昭懿 uses 謚 (posthumous name), not a temple name (廟號). Replacing “temple name” with “posthumous name” corrects the terminology while keeping the rest.
The heading 明宗和武憲皇后曹氏 again requires Empress Hewuxian; Wuhe is the same character reversal as in s0001.
Chinese ends at 不稱。」; the trailing here." after the closing quote is not in the source and breaks the English.
The literal likewise appends here." after the quotation; the Chinese speech ends at 不稱, so removing the trailing garbage is correct.
Mingzong’s speech ends at 河東。」; the trailing it?" is not in the Chinese and corrupts the sentence.
The literal’s trailing night?" has no counterpart after 河東。」 and should be removed.
明宗曰：「此羣臣之欲爾。」 ends cleanly; easier?" after the quote is invented English corruption.
Same trailing easier?" on the literal field; Chinese has nothing after the closing speech mark.
崔棁 is Cui Zhuo (棁 zhuō); Cui Rong misreads the given name. The proposed replacement corrects only that transliteration.
The literal’s Cui Rong is the same mistransliteration of 崔棁; Cui Zhuo matches the character and the unit’s pinyin.
對曰：「有之。」 has no further text; making!" after the quote is garbage absent from the Chinese.
The literal likewise appends making!" after 有之。」; removing it restores the source-faithful sentence.
釋之而不問 means he was released and the matter was not inquired into; “without punishment” understates 不問. “Without further inquiry” matches the Chinese and the unit’s literal.
字叔達 introduces the courtesy name; English needs “styled Shuda,” not ungrammatical “style Shuda.” The proposed wording matches the idiomatic field.
